title: Today: choose the next task
task: A student finds preparation and their next action.
hierarchy: Restriction notice, experiment choice, current journey state, supporting equipment list.
recovery: Unavailable kit keeps the task visible and explains the blocker.
next: Prepare E06 or E01; availability list is optional context.
question: T1: can a new student say what must happen before booking?

lines: 1 / Notice when a resource is restricted
Availability and occupancy in separate columns

research.boundary: Task-first entry is an authored choice, not a measured preference.

title: Preparation: method before reservation
task: A student reads the method and identifies kit and safety requirements.
hierarchy: Method question and source boundary, kit, acknowledgement checklist, next action.
recovery: An incomplete checklist explains why reservation cannot proceed.
next: Reserve a complete kit after preparation is acknowledged.
question: T1: can they describe the method without repeating the interface?

lines: 1 / Prepare — Reserve — Arrive — Bench — Notebook — Submit — Return
One scene / two lights / fixed settings
5 / Continue to Reserve — unmet requirements shown at action

research.boundary: Read acknowledgement is not training certification.

title: Reserve: complete-kit conflict
task: A student recovers from a booking that conflicts with one kit item.
hierarchy: Conflict reason beside times; compatible alternative and kit ownership remain visible.
recovery: 10:00 conflicts with an existing booking; choose the offered compatible slot.
question: T2: do they understand that one booking holds the whole kit?

lines: Existing booking holds part of this kit

research.boundary: Local booking policy and dependency quantities are unverified.

title: Arrive: typed ID and kit check
task: A student checks in without relying on a camera or QR scanner.
hierarchy: Station ID, check-in result, portable quantities, start-session gate.
recovery: CV-04 is refused for this booking; retain entered value and explain CV-02.
next: Check in at CV-02, verify quantities, start.
question: T4: is the wrong-station message sufficient to recover unaided?

lines: Typed ID is a first-class route
Do not assume scan means complete
Arrival and start are separate states

research.boundary: Typed path exists; physical item checks and QR devices need validation.

title: Bench: capture with context
task: A student records evidence and retains the method and source.
hierarchy: Question, evidence limitation, two conditions, record action, context link.
recovery: Interrupted camera retains recorded work and offers a labelled prepared illustration.
next: Review retained conditions or write a notebook interpretation.
question: T6: do they believe prior evidence is retained after interruption?

lines: Illustrative or generated / not a device performance measurement

research.boundary: Fixture or generated evidence is not a live device performance measurement.

title: Compare: retained conditions
task: A student inspects what changed without turning differences into causation.
hierarchy: Retained method/source/geometry, scientific plate, observations, comparison table.
recovery: Older records without context say Not recorded; current fixtures never replace them.
next: Write the student's own interpretation in the notebook.
question: U-T14: can they distinguish current scenario and recorded context?

lines: Method revision / fixture / geometry / recorded time
Field / A / B / same or different

research.boundary: Difference does not establish causation; missing context stays unknown.

title: Notebook: the student's claim
task: A student writes what the evidence supports and its limitations.
hierarchy: Prompt, editable draft, explicit save result, submission readiness.
recovery: Failed save retains draft; a draft and a saved revision are distinct.
next: Review evidence and submit a saved claim.
question: T5: do they separate samples from claims about the underlying signal?

lines: What changed? What cannot be concluded?
Draft retained during a failed save

research.boundary: The student writes the claim; no evaluated AI authoring exists.

title: Submit: pending is not complete
task: A student confirms that a submission has a receipt.
hierarchy: Evidence revision and saved claim, action, acknowledgement state, receipt.
recovery: Lost acknowledgement remains pending; retry uses the same request identity.
next: Receipt EX-SUB-2042, then close the E01 fixed-bench session. E06 separately returns its portable kit.
question: T6 extension: can they tell whether work was actually submitted?

lines: Required evidence gaps listed before completion
E01: close fixed bench / E06: return portable kit

research.boundary: Local receipt model does not prove server delivery.

title: Smart Lab: attention and context
task: Staff inspect restrictions, active work and pending acknowledgements.
hierarchy: Distinct counts, attention actions, spatial context, source-aware observations.
recovery: No sensor connection is explicit; no combined Ready or Safe score.
next: Open an equipment issue, student receipt or environment detail.
question: U-T11: can they explain why each item needs attention?

lines: 1 / Restrictions | Active sessions | Pending receipts | Connections
Each metric has its own meaning; zero connections is explicit

research.boundary: Active sessions are not learning or utilisation; this is not cohort readiness.

title: Environment: a visible boundary
task: Staff review observation freshness and booking-aware standby assumptions.
hierarchy: Scenario/source selection, observation quality, standby boundary, sustainability ledger.
recovery: Stale/invalid/missing records remain distinct; essential services excluded.
next: Human review only; no physical switching action exists.
question: U-T12 and U-T13: are source limits and booking protection understood?

lines: Temperature / CO2 / illuminance — timestamps and quality
Recyclable furniture / green materials / evidence required

research.boundary: No connected sensor, safety certification, measured savings or switch action.

title: Technician: verify before release
task: A technician handles an issue with visible consequences for bookings.
hierarchy: Issue identity, classify/restrict sequence, affected bookings, repair/verification.
recovery: Interrupted verification keeps the restriction active; release is refused.
question: T8: do they restrict before repair and understand who is affected?

lines: Report — classify — restrict — repair — verify — release

research.boundary: Demonstrated sequence requires authorised local release policy.

title: Map fallback: plan and list
task: A student finds equipment when 3D is unavailable.
hierarchy: Typed search, 2D canonical plan, text list, resource status and next action.
recovery: WebGL unavailable removes the model dependency; plan/list remain usable.
next: Inspect resource ID, availability and compatible task.
question: T3 and T7: can they locate a station without the model?

lines: 1 / Search by equipment name or typed asset ID
Geometry P4-D / assumed room / no live twin claim

research.boundary: Assumed room; plan/list preference and real circulation remain unverified.

title: Faculty: readiness before class
status: Supplementary reconstruction of original P7-A concept
task: Faculty identify a cohort support action without treating completion as learning.
hierarchy: Session identity, readiness definitions, unresolved kit/resource shortfall, named support action.
recovery: A resource shortfall remains visible; change session plan or contact the owner, not mark everyone ready.
next: Resolve the shortfall or offer preparation help; attendance is a separate task.
question: U-T15: can faculty choose a support action and explain what readiness does not prove?

lines: Definitions: prepared acknowledgement / permission / booked kit
Filter to needs help / no learning score
Attendance correction is a different record
Readiness does not establish understanding or marks

research.boundary: Learning/readiness definitions and faculty workflow need local validation.

title: Faculty: correct attendance
status: Supplementary reconstruction of original P7-A concept
task: Faculty correct a session attendance record with an explicit reason and audit history.
hierarchy: Selected session and pseudonymous record, current value, correction reason, save outcome/history.
recovery: Stale revision or failed save retains the proposed correction; reconcile current record before retry.
next: Review recorded actor, reason, time and revision; no automatic grade change.
question: U-T16: can faculty correct the intended record and tell whether it was saved?

lines: Private detail stays off public projections
Correction draft retained / reconcile current revision
Confirmation appears only after recorded success

research.boundary: No direct secondary support for the local attendance hypothesis; concept, not new React implementation.

title: Technician: record an asset move
status: Supplementary concept from original P25 movement requirement
task: A technician records a location change while keeping availability and physical handover separate.
hierarchy: Asset identity, current location, destination and reason, confirmation and movement history.
recovery: Location changed concurrently or destination unknown; retain proposal and reconcile before recording.
next: Confirm recorded movement and physical handover; restriction remains independently controlled.
question: U-T17: can a technician locate the record, propose a move and explain what availability means?

lines: 1 / Asset ID / current location / record revision
Movement does not release a restriction or verify a repair
No invented coordinates or silent overwrite

research.boundary: Source context is indirect; real inventory, destinations and movement owner need confirmation.
